stories.title: Sage-Med study: scaling medical AI models improves text, not vision
stories.summary: A new study (Sage-Med) finds that scaling medical multimodal AI models mainly improves text skills, not visual understanding, and reasoning modes fail to close the gap.
stories.more: The paper reports that existing medical multimodal large language models underperform frontier general-purpose MLLMs across a range of medical tasks. Increasing model size mainly strengthens text abilities rather than multimodal visual perception, and enabling reasoning modes does not close that visual gap. The authors describe establishing reliable scaling laws for medical MLLMs as a persistent, unresolved challenge.

Our systematic evaluation shows that existing medical MLLMs tend to underperform frontier general-purpose MLLMs across a range of medical tasks, while scaling model size primarily improves text capabilities rather than multimodal perception, and enabling reasoning modes fails to close this visual gap. stories.title: PyRUA-Dex lets coding agents learn dexterous manipulation without demos
stories.summary: Researchers present PyRUA-Dex, a framework where coding agents write programmatic policies for dexterous bimanual manipulation, avoiding costly human demonstration data.
stories.more: Progress on dexterous manipulation has been limited by scarce high-quality demonstrations: retargeting from human video is imprecise, teleoperation gives no force feedback, and exoskeleton-based collection doesn't scale. PyRUA-Dex sidesteps this by having coding agents develop a programmatic policy for the task without any demonstrations. The policy is built in two stages, the first being an exploration phase in which multiple agents explore the task.

stories.title: VibeVideoAgent closes the loop between code-driven video generation and perception
stories.summary: A new method, VibeVideoAgent, feeds rendered video frames and audio back into a coding agent so it can catch rendering errors that don't trigger runtime exceptions.
stories.more: Code-driven video generation has a coding agent write and run rendering programs, giving precise control over typography, data visualizations, synchronized audio, and multi-shot scenes while leaving an editable project behind. A program that runs without error can still produce overlapping labels, a misaimed camera, broken object interactions, or narration that drifts out of sync, none of which raise a runtime error. VibeVideoAgent addresses this by feeding the rendered frames and audio back into the coding agent, closing what the authors call the perceptual loop.

stories.title: Image-to-Video Transfer extends video editors' skills without new video data
stories.summary: A new technique, Image-to-Video Transfer (I2VT), uses an existing image editing model to upgrade pretrained video editors, adding new editing capabilities without collecting paired edited videos.
stories.more: Image editing models already follow a wide range of instructions, but video editing models lag behind in part because collecting paired source-and-edited video data is difficult. I2VT transfers advanced image-editing capabilities to video editors without needing new paired videos. It improves pretrained video editors and expands them to new editing tasks using an image editor, enabling efficient post-training with no architectural changes.

stories.title: Simon Willison quotes Scott Aaronson on AI's accelerating impact on mathematical proof
stories.summary: Simon Willison shared a quote from complexity theorist Scott Aaronson describing recent progress as revealing 'a whole new continent of mathematical truth' once only glimpsed through fog.
stories.more: Aaronson compares the shift to van Leeuwenhoek first training a microscope on pondwater, or Galileo first turning a telescope on the stars, as an analogy for how much better humanity's view into the complexity-theoretic and mathematical universe has recently become.

items.title: Quoting Scott Aaronson
items.excerpt: It’s now obvious that we’ll be getting, not one-off solutions to this or that complexity question, but a whole new continent of mathematical truth, one that we’d previously only glimpsed through fog. Picture van Leeuwenhoek first training a microscope on pondwater, or Galileo first training his telescope on the stars. That might give you some idea of how our resolution into the complexity-theoretic universe, and the whole universe of mathematical truth beyond it, has now improved. — Scott Aarons

stories.title: ICLWorld benchmarks in-context learning for agents across digital and physical tasks
stories.summary: ICLWorld is a new online benchmark testing how well AI agents use in-context learning to adapt in real time, spanning both computer-use and robotic tasks.
stories.more: In-context learning lets agents pick up new rules from context and adapt to user-specific requirements at inference time, and the same frontier agents now operate both computers and robots. The authors argue this ability is still poorly assessed: existing benchmarks are largely offline, rely on text or static images, and risk training-data contamination, while robot evaluations are limited to method-level ablations. ICLWorld is introduced as an online benchmark that evaluates agents' in-context learning from digital to physical settings.

stories.title: Anthropic's Amodei pushes back on claims AI should be allowed to govern society
stories.summary: Dario Amodei rejected an Axios report suggesting some employees believe humanity should hand power to superintelligent AI, calling such accusations 'absurd' and AI governance of society 'a bad idea.'
stories.more: The pushback responds to an Axios report describing employees who reportedly believe humanity will eventually hand power to superintelligent AI systems. Amodei called accusations that he favors surrendering human agency to AI 'absurd,' even as leading AI companies increasingly automate their own research and model development. He separately stated that 'turning over governance to AI is a bad idea.'

stories.title: Amazon and Meta reportedly in talks to end block on shopping agent Muse
stories.summary: Amazon and Meta are discussing ending the block on Meta's AI shopping agent Muse, which Amazon removed from its platform in September amid a dispute over ad revenue and search control.

stories.title: AIRIS benchmark tests embodied agents' social judgment in streaming video
stories.summary: AIRIS is a new causal, streaming benchmark that evaluates whether embodied AI agents can read social cues and decide when, whether, and how to respond around people.
stories.more: Embodied agents operating around people must recognize social cues and also judge when evidence is sufficient, whether to intervene, and how to respond without breaking social norms. Existing benchmarks typically test these abilities in isolation or only on completed videos, which obscures exactly where an online social decision goes wrong. AIRIS instead frames social embodied intelligence as a time-anchored, causal chain of attention, intention, and response, evaluated on egocentric streaming video.

stories.title: OpenAI's Thariq Shihipar on AI enabling both cheap software and crafted work
stories.summary: At the AI Engineer CODE conference, OpenAI's Thariq Shihipar argued AI can make software cheap to produce at scale while also freeing up time to make individual work feel right.
stories.more: Shihipar framed this as a choice between 'the Revolution' and 'the Renaissance': AI letting software be produced cheaply by the thousand, versus giving creators more time to refine a single piece of work. He argued the two futures can coexist rather than compete. As an example from his own fighting game project, he described editing the size of a rock using AI tooling.

stories.title: Simon Willison highlights sqlite3_rsync, a remote-copy tool for SQLite databases
stories.summary: Simon Willison wrote about sqlite3_rsync, an experimental SQLite tool for copying databases remotely without needing extra disk space for a full duplicate, unlike the backup API or VACUUM INTO.
stories.more: The tool has existed for a while, added as 'experimental' in SQLite 3.47.0 in October 2024 and enhanced in SQLite 3.50.0 in May 2025. Willison notes that normally grabbing a snapshot copy of a SQLite database requires either the backup API or VACUUM INTO, both of which need enough free disk space to hold a full duplicate copy.
